config.title: Cranes Near Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: When the cranes are at Linum, what time they fly in, and how to get there and back by train, bus or bike.

items.q: When is the best time to see the cranes at Linum?
items.a: The season runs from **mid September into November**. Between 2018 and 2025 the highest weekly count fell between 30 September and 31 October, most often in the middle of October, with 42,740 to 79,240 cranes at the Linum roost. Early in the season there are fewer visitors, and weekdays are quieter than weekends.

items.q: What time do the cranes fly in at Linum?
items.a: They fly in to roost as the light goes. The local association's rule of thumb is from about **17:00 before the clocks change on 25 October** and from about **16:00 after**, with birds arriving until it is dark. Sunset at Linum is 18:42 on 3 October, 18:10 on 17 October and 16:28 on 7 November.

items.q: Can I get to Linum by public transport at the weekend?
items.a: Not by bus this season. The VBB timetable shows no bus to Linum on Saturdays, Sundays or public holidays, and the weekend crane bus of earlier years is not running. The practical option is the train to **Kremmen** and an 11 km bike ride. Trains leave Kremmen for Hennigsdorf twice an hour until 22:56.

items.q: How do I get to Linum by bus on a weekday?
items.a: Take the RE8 from Berlin Hauptbahnhof to Nauen and bus 758 to Linum, Küsterstege. The 14:25 from Hauptbahnhof arrives at 15:30. The last direct bus back leaves at **18:24**, at Hauptbahnhof at 19:35. Before 25 October that is before it is dark, so take the **19:30** via Fehrbellin and Neuruppin instead, at Hauptbahnhof at 21:49.

items.q: Does the Deutschlandticket cover the trip to Linum?
items.a: Yes, for you. It covers the regional trains, the S-Bahn and the buses. It does not cover a bike: a VBB single bike ticket for the whole network costs **€4.60** each way, or €7.50 for 24 hours.

items.q: Where is the best place to watch the cranes at Linum?
items.a: The local association recommends three spots for the evening fly-in: the Schöpfwerk pumping station, walking out along the Koppelweg that branches off it; the meadow behind the village church; and the pond area. By day the cranes feed on the fields along the Kuhhorster Weg. Never enter fields, farm tracks or the nature reserve.

items.q: Are there guided crane tours at Linum?
items.a: Yes. NABU's Storchenschmiede at Nauener Straße 54 runs evening fly-in tours of about 90 minutes for **€10** (€8 reduced) and morning tours for €12, with booking required. In the crane season, 18 September to 1 November, the exhibition is open Friday to Sunday from 11:00 until an hour after sunset.
